The principle “process the smaller half” then implies that every state and transition is only visited O(log n) times. However, we do not know a priori which of the three parts are the smallest. Therefore, we start four coroutines for the four parts, run them in lockstep and abort the coroutine that belongs to the largest part. This ensures that time proportional to the three smallest parts is used. Preconditions. At least one splitter must be non-empty. If both splitters are given (as in line 1.18 of Algorithm 1), it is known that every bottom state of B has a transition in at least one of the two splitters. We use data structures such that it is possible to quickly determine whether states with a transition in SmallSp also have a transition in LargeSp.
